top3.why: Learn to build a home page like it's 1999 — Ragman (Richard Green) walks you through the basics of HTML and gets you a static site live on Neocities by the end of the night. No experience necessary, and it's pay-what-you-can ($10–$25 suggested, no one turned away for lack of funds). It's the hands-on, unpretentious tech education that makes Iffy Books one of the city's best-kept secrets.

NYC noise-rock institution Oneida brings its 17th album, Expensive Air, to Johnny Brenda's alongside fellow genre-benders Kinski — two bands who've spent decades proving a song can be pushed past its structure into something harder and stranger. $25.65, doors at 7.

One PA's West/Southwest Rising throws its annual cookout in Malcolm X Park, building working-class power in West and Southwest Philly over free food and community. It's the rare organizing event that comes with dinner and a cookout instead of folding chairs in a church basement.

cinéSPEAK screens the 1994 narrative feature at Two Locals Brewing.
Texas-born singer-songwriter with a Grammy nomination for co-writing John Legend's ‘Conversations in the Dark.’
Linocut carving workshop — carve and print your own patches at this community print shop and zine library.
Monthly community meeting at Kol Tzedek building tenant and neighbor power in West/Southwest Philly; dinner provided.
Weekly jazz/soul jam session hosted by Richard Hill Jr. and friends at Black Squirrel Club.
Volunteer stewardship morning pulling invasives and litter at Cobbs Creek Park, plus a short ecology walk and talk.

top3.why: A West Philly debut for the new Del Rossi Trio, a solo drone set from Search for the Infinite Light, and a rare solo-voice performance from Kilynn Lunsford — curated by Yoni Kroll in the intimate upstairs room at Abyssinia, with excellent Ethiopian food downstairs. $10–15, 21+, and about as far from a typical Tuesday as it gets.

A reading group digging into Bayard Rustin's ‘Freedom Budget for All Americans’ — the jobs-centric economic vision from the organizer who actually built the March on Washington that MLK spoke at. Free, discussion-driven, and a genuinely different angle on a civil rights figure most people only know from one speech.

top3.address: 1400 John F Kennedy Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19107
top3.why: A landlord's letter threatening to sell 925 affordable units in West and Southwest Philly to a private developer could displace thousands of tenants — this rally at City Hall demands the city and owner keep the properties affordable. Free, urgent, and exactly the kind of unglamorous fight that decides whether a neighborhood stays livable.

Free outdoor concert series at FDR Park's lakes; this week's set is Gumbo Nouveau.

Philadelphia Area Horror Meetup Group streams the beloved body-horror B-movie Basket Case.
Beginner-friendly swing dance classes rooted in Philly's Lindy Hop community; no partner needed.

top3.why: Build a tiny solar-powered square-wave synth on a breadboard — no soldering required, just a $12.50 kit and curiosity. It's DIY electronics at its most playful, the kind of low-stakes maker project that turns into a real skill by the end of the night.

Kieślowski's towering ten-part meditation on the Ten Commandments gets a rare 4K theatrical run, two parts at a time. Parts 1 and 2 open with a father questioning faith through his son's eyes and a woman torn between a dying husband and an unborn child — as intimate and devastating as cinema gets.

Philly DSA canvasses West Philly for Chris Rabb, a democratic socialist running for PA-03 on universal healthcare, childcare, and abolishing ICE. No experience needed — new canvassers get trained and paired with a partner, then there's a debrief hang after.

top3.why: A touring showcase of horror shorts directed, written, or produced by women and non-binary filmmakers, with festival founder Sara Neidorf in attendance. It's horror without the usual victim-camera-fantasy math — messier, weirder, and told from the other side of the knife.

A free double feature of Chilean director Sebastián Silva's Rotting in the Sun and Tyrel at the Rotunda, one of the city's great free/PWYW film venues. Two hours of uncomfortable, funny, formally sharp filmmaking for the price of showing up.

Progressive post-hardcore quartet Hail the Sun bring their intricate, high-energy sound to Union Transfer — a band that built a decade-plus career on refusing to just scream through intense emotion when a melody would hit harder.

top3.why: Filmmaker Alex Cox is in attendance for a screening of his punk sci-fi classic Repo Man, followed by a live set from the actual Circle Jerks — LA hardcore royalty who've been playing since 1979 and share a founding member with Black Flag. Doors 7, film and show 8; this is the rare night where the movie and the band are both the headliner.

The Red Rabbis run their monthly De-Escalation 101 at Wooden Shoe Books, teaching practical tools for staying grounded and co-regulating through conflict on the ground. Built for organizers and public workers alike; masks required and provided, free.

Nicolas Winding Refn's guerrilla 1996 debut — and Mads Mikkelsen's first-ever feature — gets a brand-new 4K restoration as the opener of PFS's full Pusher trilogy retrospective. Copenhagen's underworld has rarely looked this grimy or this good.

Philly's only video-game jazz fusion quintet plays retro soundtracks while you play retro games; free entry.

top3.why: An interactive training on tenant rights and what to actually do in the face of eviction, hosted at Philly's anarchist bookstore. Practical, free, and the kind of skill-building that matters far more than another rally.

The self-described world's largest traveling oddities show rolls into Oaks with taxidermy, preserved specimens, quack medical devices, skulls, and handmade horror-inspired art from vendors who take the weird seriously. Everything's legal and sustainably sourced — a full day for anyone who'd rather browse bone jewelry than a mall.

Philly's #1 post-punk party for over 15 years — Depeche Mode, Joy Division, New Order, The Smiths, The Cure, and everything post-punk/darkwave/goth adjacent, spun to a packed dance floor with free pretzels while they last. $7 advance, $10 at the door, 10pm start.

top3.why: Charles Burnett's landmark 1978 portrait of a working-class Black man's life in 1970s LA, blending cinéma vérité with Italian neorealism, gets a rare 4K theatrical screening as part of PFS's LA Rebellion series. One of the most quietly devastating films in American independent cinema, and not one that plays theaters often.

Richmond crust/hardcore band Skeksis headlines a stacked DIY bill of hardcore punk at Cousin Danny's, with local support from Nightfall, Sediment, and Diskritik. No frills, no barrier, just a house-show-adjacent room and four bands that mean it.

Blood Sick Underground Cinema premieres director Kasper Meltedhair's aggressively strange no-budget sci-fi at PhilaMOCA, the city's home for underground and outsider film. Come for the plot synopsis alone — it will not make more sense after you've seen it, and that's the point.
